blocks.text: Pichhle sabaq mein humne dekha ke perpendicular vectors ka dot product zero hota hai. Ab yahi baat ek test (pehchan) ban jati hai. Space mein do vectors perpendicular hain ya nahin, yeh aankh se ya protractor se dekhna mumkin nahin; lekin dot product components se foran nikal aata hai. Isi liye yeh test poori vector algebra mein sab se zyada istemal hota hai.
Definition: do non-zero vectors \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) perpendicular hain agar aur sirf agar (if and only if) \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\) ho.

Kyun ke \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ke darmiyan angle \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) (yani \(90^{\circ}\)) hai aur \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\), is liye

\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
\[\therefore\ \underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\]

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Kyun ke har vector \(\underline{b}\) ke liye \(\underline{0} \cdot \underline{b} = 0\), is liye zero vector ko har vector ke perpendicular maana jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"If and only if" ka matlab hai ke baat dono taraf chalti hai: perpendicular hon to dot product zero; aur dot product zero ho (aur dono vectors non-zero hon) to perpendicular. "Orthogonal" perpendicular ka hi doosra naam hai.
Note wali baat ajeeb lagti hai, magar wajah saada hai: zero vector ki koi simt hi nahin, is liye us ka dot product hamesha zero aata hai. Isi liye definition mein "non-zero" likha hai, taa ke yeh khaas soorat alag rahe.

(i) Agar \(\theta = 0\) ya \(\pi\) ho, to vectors \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) collinear (ek hi line par) hain.
(ii) Agar \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\) ho, to \(\cos\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\).
Is liye vectors \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) perpendicular ya orthogonal hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Corollary (i) mein vectors ek hi line par hain: \(\theta = 0\) par dono ek simt mein (\(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\)), aur \(\theta = \pi\) par ulti simt mein (\(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = -|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\)). Yani parallel vectors ka dot product sab se bara ya sab se chhota hota hai, aur perpendicular ka bilkul zero.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice, kitab ka sawal nahin.) Kya \(\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\) aur \(4\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) perpendicular hain?
\[(1)(4) + (2)(1) + (3)(-2) = 4 + 2 - 6 = 0\]
Haan! Dot product zero hai aur dono non-zero hain, is liye yeh perpendicular hain, halaan ke dekhne mein in mein koi rishta nazar nahin aata.

blocks.title: Example 9
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = 3\underline{i} - \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}\).
To find: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\).
Method: sab se pehle components saaf likh lete hain, signs samet: \(\underline{u}\) ke \((3, -1, -2)\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ke \((1, 2, -1)\). Ghor karein: \(-\underline{j}\) ka matlab coefficient \(-1\) hai. Phir 14.2.5 ka formula: matching components multiply, phir jama.

Step 1: Matching components multiply kar ke jama
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = (3)(1) + (-1)(2) + (-2)(-1)\]
\[= 3 - 2 + 2 = 3\]
Kyun: formula \(a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2}\) hai. Har product bracket mein likha taa ke koi sign gum na ho. Teesre term mein minus guna minus plus hua: \((-2)(-1) = +2\).

Tasdeeq:
Tarteeb ulat kar dekhein: \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{u} = (1)(3) + (2)(-1) + (-1)(-2) = 3\). Wahi jawab, kyun ke dot product commutative hai. Jawab positive hai, yani in ke darmiyan angle acute hai, perpendicular nahin.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem: If \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{v} = 4\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\), then prove that \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\) are orthogonal.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = 4\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\).
To prove: \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) orthogonal (perpendicular) hain.
Method: space mein angle naapna mushkil hai, protractor kaam nahin aata. Lekin humare paas test hai: do non-zero vectors tabhi perpendicular hain jab un ka dot product \(0\) ho. To bas \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) nikaal kar dekhte hain.

Step 1: Dot product nikaalein
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = (2)(4) + (-4)(-3) + (5)(-4)\]
\[= 8 + 12 - 20 = 0\]
Kyun: 14.2.5 ka component formula. Dhyan dein: \((-4)(-3) = +12\), yahan sign ki ghalti bohat aam hai.

Step 2: Nateeja
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0 \Rightarrow \underline{u} \perp \underline{v}\]
Kyun: dono vectors non-zero hain (in ke components zero nahin), is liye \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}| \ne 0\). To \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta = 0\) tabhi ho sakta hai jab \(\cos\theta = 0\), yani \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\).

Tasdeeq:
Dono vectors waqai non-zero hain: \(|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{4 + 16 + 25} = \sqrt{45}\), \(|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{16 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{41}\). Is liye zero dot product sirf right angle ki wajah se hai.
blocks.answer: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\), is liye \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) perpendicular (orthogonal) hain. Saabit ho gaya.

blocks.title: Example 11
blocks.problem: Find a scalar \(\alpha\) so that the vectors \(2\underline{i} + \alpha\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) and \(3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \alpha\underline{k}\) are orthogonal.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} + \alpha\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \alpha\underline{k}\), aur yeh orthogonal hain.
To find: \(\alpha\).
Method: yahan sawal ulta hai: perpendicular hona diya hua hai aur ek component maloom nahin. Perpendicular ka matlab \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\); is se \(\alpha\) ki ek equation ban jayegi jise hal kar lenge.

Step 1: Shart likhein
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\]
\[(2\underline{i} + \alpha\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}) \cdot (3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \alpha\underline{k}) = 0\]
Kyun: orthogonal vectors ki definition yahi hai.

Step 2: Kholiye
\[(2)(3) + (\alpha)(1) + (5)(\alpha) = 0\]
\[6 + \alpha + 5\alpha = 0\]
Kyun: matching components multiply kar ke jama. \(\alpha\) ek aam number ki tarah hi multiply hota hai.

Step 3: Hal karein
\[6\alpha = -6 \Rightarrow \alpha = -1\]
Kyun: \(\alpha\) wale terms jama kiye (\(\alpha + 5\alpha = 6\alpha\)), \(6\) doosri taraf gaya to \(-6\) bana, phir \(6\) se divide.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab ke Example 11 mein line \(\Rightarrow (2\underline{i} + \alpha\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}) \cdot (3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \alpha\underline{k})\) ke aage "\(= 0\)" chhapne se reh gaya hai. Asal equation \((\dots) \cdot (\dots) = 0\) hai, jaisa humare Step 1 mein likha hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 11 mein agar \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) hota (yani \(\alpha\) sirf \(\underline{u}\) mein), to \(\alpha\) kya aata? Sochiye: \(6 + \alpha + 10 = 0\), yani \(\alpha = -16\). Tareeqa wahi: dot product zero rakho aur equation hal karo.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Non-zero vectors ke liye: \(\underline{u} \perp \underline{v} \iff \underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\).
2. Zero vector har vector ke perpendicular maana jata hai.
3. Kisi unknown ko aisa banana ho ke vectors perpendicular hon: dot product \(= 0\) rakh kar equation hal karein.
4. Collinear vectors: \(\theta = 0\) ya \(\pi\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Products ke sign mein ghalti, jaise \((-4)(-3)\) ko \(-12\) likh dena; ek sign ghalat ho to zero chhup jata hai.
2. Perpendicular ke liye dot product ko \(1\) ke barabar rakh dena; sahi \(0\) hai.
3. Parallel aur perpendicular ko mila dena: parallel mein \(\theta = 0\) ya \(\pi\), perpendicular mein \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
4. \(-\underline{j}\) ka coefficient \(0\) samajh lena; woh \(-1\) hai.
